title: Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: A strong business can still be a poor entry.
epigraph.author: Market maxim

book_paragraphs: The technical record is mixed across timeframes. A separate TheWrap leaderboard feed records 82 weeks of Stage 2 membership, a 274.3% cumulative stage return and top-25 list inclusion. The current market_facts trend filter classifies the chart as Stage 3 (Topping/Pullback), while the separate stock_snapshot timing filter classifies it as Stage 4 with an AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN posture. These filters use different stage rules; the more restrictive no-entry rule controls. The historical leaderboard record is not a current entry signal. The recent drawdown reinforces that distinction: the close was down 14.5% over one week, 24.6% over one month and 15.5% over three months, while remaining up 61.9% over one year. This is a former leader undergoing a sharp correction, not a clean momentum entry [1].

At ₹625.90, the share closed below its daily 10-, 20- and 50-day averages of ₹653, ₹678 and ₹731, and below its weekly 30-week SMA of ₹663 and 10-week EMA of ₹688. It remained above the 200-day SMA near ₹590 and above the longer weekly 40-week EMA near ₹608. The structure says short-term supply has overwhelmed demand while the longer trend has not fully broken. Daily RSI at 41.4 and weekly RSI at 47.5 show weak to neutral momentum, not an oversold capitulation reading [1].

The first shelf is the ₹599–₹610 area, where the TradingView daily S1 pivot at ₹599.53 overlaps the 200-day average. That makes it a plausible demand zone to observe, not a guaranteed floor. A close below the shelf, followed by failure to reclaim it, would shift attention to the next support region around ₹485, close to the daily S2 pivot. The base plan uses ₹520 as invalidation, below the first shelf but above the deeper pivot, leaving room for ordinary volatility while recognizing that a decisive break would invalidate the support thesis [1].

The 4-hour chart does not yet confirm a turn. The 4-hour RSI is 43.1 compared with daily RSI 41.4, but the share price at ₹625.90 is below the 4-hour EMA20 near ₹646, and the engine flags no intraday 4-hour turn. A better setup would include a higher low above ₹599, a reclaim of the 4-hour EMA20, and then a move back over the daily 20-day average. These are confirmation conditions; the report does not infer a reversal from one positive day after a deep monthly decline [1].

Volume deserves caution. The session volume was about 2.16 times the 30-day average, but a high-volume day after a 24.6% one-month decline can represent selling as easily as accumulation. We do not label it institutional buying without a sustained sequence of higher-volume advances, rising relative strength versus the Nifty, and improving delivery evidence. The Stage 2 snapshot supports a longer-term leader classification; the failed market-wide scanner means we cannot compare that leadership against fresh sector breadth or distribution-day counts in this report [1].

The tactical judgment is therefore patient. The business quality gate is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL, not a price trigger. The broad stage remains constructive, but the stock’s short-term structure is damaged: price sits below key short and intermediate averages, and the 4-hour recovery has not confirmed. A pullback and stabilization between ₹585 and ₹600, followed by a weekly close back above the shelf and the 20-day average, would improve the setup. A decisive weekly close below ₹520 would cancel the setup and send the investor back to fundamental review rather than averaging down [1].

The options overlay is deliberately simple. TDPOWERSYS is not in the NSE F&O segment and the snapshot found no liquid listed options chain, so there is no defensible call spread or LEAPS payoff to quote. The options status is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID; any position is cash equity with full downside exposure. The user’s Chrome session had no open TradingView chart, so the read used public TradingView data and the same-session stock snapshot. Do not read this options panel as a recommendation to trade a derivative [1].

For a new position, the proposed entry band is ₹585–₹600, with an alert-only invalidation at ₹520 and a two-year base value of ₹820. At the top of the entry band, base-case reward is ₹220 per share versus ₹80 of defined risk, or 2.75:1. The probability-weighted scenario value is lower than the base target but still above the entry band; the mechanical sizing table below uses the portfolio’s tier risk budget and applies no allocation until the entry and confirmation gates are met. At the current close, estimated upside to the base value is about 31%, but risk to the stop is about 17%, and timing remains unresolved. Patience is part of the edge [1].

Here is how I would use the chart in practice. First, mark the ₹599–₹610 shelf and the 200-day average around ₹590. Then wait for the stock to spend time there without repeated high-volume closes below support. A single intraday wick does not count as a hold. Next, look for a higher low and a close above the 4-hour EMA20; only after that would a reclaim of the daily 20-day average near ₹678 begin to repair the medium-term chart. Finally, compare relative strength with the Nifty and the electrical-equipment group. This sequence avoids turning the first bounce into proof of a new uptrend.

The volume ratio of 2.16x is an observation, not a buy signal. In a rising stock, repeated above-average volume on advances and lighter volume on pullbacks can support accumulation. In this case, the ratio arrives after a steep monthly decline, so it can equally reflect supply hitting bids. We do not have the market-wide delivery and sector-flow extraction because the dashboard scanner failed. The correct conclusion is narrow: activity was unusually high, but its direction cannot be inferred from volume alone. A future session series with delivery data and relative-strength improvement would raise confidence.

The No-FOMO table expresses sizing as a ceiling, not an instruction to spend that amount. The portfolio’s tier risk budget translates the stop distance into a theoretical weight, but this dossier assigns no present allocation because both the timing gate and the support retest remain open. If price gaps through ₹520, the planned risk is not guaranteed: a stop may execute lower, and the investor could lose more than the modeled unit. Use limit discipline, accept missed trades, and size from the distance between entry and invalidation rather than from the number of shares you hope to own.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A trend label describes the longer chart. An entry decision asks whether demand has returned at the price you can actually buy. Here the trend is still alive on the weekly scale, but the short chart has not repaired. Waiting for a higher low and a reclaim is a way to let buyers prove they are back.
